newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - December 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - December 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- A team of the European Commission will come to Pakistan next February in connection with anti-dumping inquiry relating to bed-linen exports.
- The arrest of Shaukat Kazmi, president of private Allied Bank Ltd has resulted in the withdrawal of two billion rupees from the bank.
- The State Bank of Pakistan has asked banks to publish annual accounts on time.
- Chief of the Army Staff General Jehangir Karamat called on President Farooq Leghari and discussed the general political situation.
- The caretaker government has reaffirmed its determination to take action against corrupt politicians and bureaucrats before February 3 elections.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government intends to deregulate the prices of petroleum products at the retail stage shortly.

- In order to roll over all the maturities, the State (central) Bank of Pakistan raised the cut-off in the short term federal bond auction to 17.25 percent in the latest auction compared to 16.50 percent in the auction held two weeks ago.
FINANCIAL POST
- India is willing to exchange tea with Pakistan engineering goods, says Iftikhar Ali Malik, vice-president of the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry.
THE NATION

- The Pakistani and Indian chambers of commerce and industry on Monday signed a memorandum of understanding to work together to support and promote the buisness interest of private sector of both the countries on reciprocal basis.
- The government has amended the recently promulgted Accountability Ordinance to bring in to its net heads and deputy heads and officials of local bodies.
- At least 50 people were injured when five bogies of Karachi-bound Shalimar Express train derailed near Sahiwal.
THE NEWS
- The government has re-constituted the Privatisation Commission.

- The government has allowed a delegation of 200 Pakistani intellectuals, writers and artistes to travel to India by road to participate in Pakistan-India Forum's convention being held in the Indian city of Calcutta.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
